# Interpreter code read by the shared read-only rule: the gate reads it to
# decide whether to ask, and the approval card reads it to decide whether the
# countdown may run. Each line is a verdict ("read" or "refuse"), a vertical
# bar, and one line of Python. Both sides run this same corpus, so a verdict
# that holds on one side and not the other shows up here.
read|import json
read|import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin))
read|import os; print(os.environ['HOME'])
read|import os; print(os.environ.get('X'))
read|import os; p = os.environ['TMPDIR'] + '/x'; print(open(p).read())
read|import html,os; print(html.unescape(os.environ['HOME']))
read|import sys; print(sys.stdin.read())
read|open('x')
read|open('x',encoding='utf-8')
read|open('x','r')
read|open('x','rb')
read|for i,line in enumerate(open('x',encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore'),1): print(i)
read|import re; print(re.search('a','a'))
read|print('os')
read|print('sys')
read|print('use os.system here')
refuse|import os; os.system('id')
refuse|import os; os.remove('/tmp/x')
refuse|import sys; sys.exit()
refuse|import os; f = os; f.remove('/tmp/x')
refuse|import os; f = os; f.execv('/bin/sh', ['sh'])
refuse|import os as o; o.remove('/x')
refuse|from os import system
read|from os import environ as env; print(env['HOME'])

refuse|import socket
refuse|import httpx
refuse|getattr(__builtins__,'x')
refuse|open('x','w')
